fact: 1916年5月维也纳爆发首次粮食骚乱：骚乱于5月11日从第10区Eugenplatz市场开始，随后数日蔓延至Rudolfsheim与Schmelz等区；5月18日维也纳警察总局的报告记录示威者高喊“我们饿了，孩子也跟着我们挨饿，给我们吃的，打倒抬价的人，我们要和平”。警察大规模逮捕并在全市实施宵禁，新闻检查压制了报道。

sources.title: Die Welt der Habsburger（奥地利科学院/维也纳市立图书馆合作项目），“Hunger and protest”
sources.quote: In Vienna in May 1916 the first food disturbances occurred. Groups of emaciated youths plundered food wagons and smashed in shop windows, women formed into protest chains and marched towards the central district to declare their anger. The police reacted with a wave of arrests and imposed a curfew on the city.

sources.title: Die Welt der Habsburger，“Hunger and protest”（引维也纳警察总局1916年5月18日报告）
sources.quote: On May 18, 1916 the Austro-Hungarian police directorate noted: ‘The excited mood of the population resulted on the 11 of the month in clashes (hunger riots) at the market at Eugenplatz in the X. Distr. [sic!] which spread to the districts of Rudolfsheim and Schmelz in the following days.

sources.title: Cahiers bruxellois, “From the Brilliant Metropolis of a Great Power to the ‘Swelled Head’ of a Rump State: Vienna in the First World War”
sources.quote: In May 1916 demonstrations and riots ("hunger riots") occurred all over Vienna and in the periphery. Shop displays were damaged by stones as were also trams in one depot.

fact: 1916年奥匈设立食品局（Ernährungsamt），作为准部级的国家机构统一协调食品供应、分配与定价；同年配给卡从面包、面粉扩大到糖、牛奶、咖啡与油脂（马铃薯与果酱在1917年、肉类在1918年才纳入）。

sources.title: 1914-1918-Online, “Social Conflict and Control, Protest and Repression (Austria-Hungary)”
sources.quote: To manage the food crisis, the Food Office, a quasi-ministerial state-level institution was created in 1916 to coordinate food supply, distribution and pricing.

sources.title: Die Welt der Habsburger，“Managing the shortages”
sources.quote: Gradually the card system was extended to other foodstuffs, too: in 1916 the rationing of sugar, milk, coffee and fat followed, and later on that of potatoes, meat and jam.

sources.title: 1914-1918-Online, “Social Conflict and Control, Protest and Repression (Austria-Hungary)”
sources.quote: the first ration cards appeared in April 1915 for flour and bread, followed by sugar, milk, coffee and lard in 1916, potatoes and marmalade in 1917 and meat in 1918

fact: 1916年6月4日布鲁西洛夫攻势开始：俄军西南方面军当日先在塔尔诺波尔与切尔诺夫策方向突击，6月5日在卢茨克方向击溃奥匈第4集团军防线；至6月20日俄军俘获20万人，至8月俘奥军37.5万人，奥匈失去布科维纳与东加利西亚大部。俄军自身在战役中损失约100万人（含大量逃兵与俘虏）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “World War I: The Eastern Front, 1916”
sources.quote: Brusilov undertook to start his attack on June 4, on the understanding that Evert’s should be launched 10 days later. ... By June 20, Brusilov’s forces had captured 200,000 prisoners. ... Brusilov had driven the Austrians from Bukovina and from much of eastern Galicia and had inflicted huge losses of men and equipment on them, but he had depleted Russia’s armies by about 1,000,000 men in doing so.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Aleksey Alekseyevich Brusilov”
sources.quote: From June 4, 1916, Brusilov led these armies, who were billeted south of the Pripet Marshes, in a massive attack against the Austro-Hungarian forces. Though they suffered heavy losses, Brusilov’s forces by August had taken 375,000 Austrian prisoners (200,000 in the first three days of the offensive) and had overrun all of Bukovina and part of eastern Galicia.

fact: 弗朗茨·约瑟夫一世于1916年11月21日去世，侄孙卡尔一世同日继位，在位至1918年11月11日；即位后卡尔通过妻弟西克斯图斯亲王向协约国秘密试探单独媾和，因拒绝向意大利割让领土而失败，1917年其求和信被公开后在国内与德国均受损。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Charles (I)”
sources.quote: the last ruler of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy (November 21, 1916–November 11, 1918)

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Charles (I)”
sources.quote: After his accession, Charles, a peace-loving man, made attempts to take Austria-Hungary out of World War I through secret overtures to the Allied powers, the most promising being through his brother-in-law, Prince Sixtus von Bourbon-Parma. All failed, largely because the emperor refused to cede any territories to Italy.

fact: 1916年哈布斯堡帝国人均面包谷物消费降至118公斤（1909—1913年平均为184公斤，1915年为136公斤）；同年匈牙利可供奥地利的谷物不足10万吨，而战前匈牙利每年向奥地利出口超过200万吨。

sources.title: 1914-1918-Online, “Food and Nutrition (Austria-Hungary)”
sources.quote: The average consumption of bread grains per head in the Habsburg Empire decreased steadily compared to the pre-war level (1909/13: 184 kg, 1914: 134 kg, 1915: 136 kg, 1916: 118 kg, 1917: 132 kg, 1918: 101 kg).

sources.title: 1914-1918-Online, “Austria-Hungary”
sources.quote: Hungary, which had annually exported over 2 million tons of grain to Austria, now had to feed the military (over 3 million enlisted men and draft animals). By 1916 Hungary could barely spare 100,000 tons for Austria.

fact: 维也纳配给按“自给者／非自给者／重体力工人”三类发放：配给卡推行时非自给者每日1,300千卡、重体力工人1,725千卡，而战前维也纳工人平均摄入2,845千卡；配给卡上的数量在零售店常常买不到，实际到手的卡路里低于卡面。

sources.title: Die Welt der Habsburger，“Managing the shortages”
sources.quote: while heavy workers had at least 1,725 calories, and non-self-providers 1,300 calories daily, the allocated quota eventually sank to 1,290 and 830 calories per day respectively.

sources.title: 1914-1918-Online, “Social Conflict and Control, Protest and Repression (Austria-Hungary)”
sources.quote: At the time when ration cards were introduced for various foodstuffs, “non-self-providing” consumers (a category based on the kind of work one did) were allotted 1,300 calories per day.

sources.title: 1914-1918-Online, “Food and Nutrition (Austria-Hungary)”
sources.quote: Compared to the average intake of a Viennese worker of 2,845 kilocalories in the pre-war era, the official ration at the end of war had shrunk dramatically to 1,293 kilocalories (-81 percent) for normal “non-self-supporters” and 831 kilocalories (-55 percent) for “heavy workers.”

fact: 奥地利一侧（内莱塔尼亚）面粉每公斤官方价1914年为0.44克朗、1915年约0.80克朗、1916年夏约0.99克朗；同一时期黑市价约为官价的5倍，且按官价“有钱也买不到”。该组数字来自俄文二手综述，未取得奥地利官方统计原件。

sources.title: Военное обозрение（Topwar），“Austria-Hungary in the war: 1916 and 1917 campaigns. Deterioration of the empire”
sources.quote: A kilogram of flour in Zisleletania in the summer of 1914 cost an average of 0,44 crowns, a year later - 0,80, and in the summer of 1916 years - 0,99 crowns. And it was extremely difficult to buy it for this money, and on the black market (it appeared in 1915), a kilogram of flour could cost 5 times more.

sources.title: Die Welt der Habsburger，“Managing the shortages”
sources.quote: In practice, however, these upper limits developed into minimal prices, and traders continued to withhold their products or to sell them on the black market at a multiple of the regular prices.

fact: 奥地利议会自1914年春解散后直到1917年5月才复会，1916年全年奥地利一侧实际以官僚机构与紧急状态下的行政命令统治；同年食品配给把居民按“自给者（有农地牲畜）／非自给者（城市购买者）”分类，身份类别直接决定可领取的配额。

sources.title: 1914-1918-Online, “Social Conflict and Control, Protest and Repression (Austria-Hungary)”
sources.quote: The Austrian parliament had been dissolved in the spring of 1914 and did not convene again until May 1917. Political parties and their publications (notably of Slavs and leftists) were heavily censored.

sources.title: Die Welt der Habsburger，“Managing the shortages”
sources.quote: The food cards were given out according to three categories and differentiated between self-providers (agricultural producers), non-self-providers (the urban population) and heavy workers (pooled together in this category were industrial workers, railway employees and security officials).

fact: 克朗在1916年同时对内对外贬值：奥匈银行纸币流通从1914年7月23日的21.60亿克朗增至1916年12月31日的108.90亿克朗；克朗对瑞士法郎的汇率（每100克朗）从平价105法郎跌至1916年6月的66.75法郎。

sources.title: Federal Reserve Bulletin, April 1918, “Loans Issued in Period 1914–1917”（FRASER 转录，引奥匈银行报告）
sources.quote: Notes in circulation increased from 2,160 million crowns on July 23, 1914, to 18,440 millions on December 31, 1917, an increase of 15,580 million crowns. ... Dec. 31, 1914 5,200 Dec. 31, 1915 7,200 Dec. 31, 1916 10,890

sources.title: “The Central-European Economic Effects of the World War I”（Kaposvár University 论文，Table 3）
sources.quote: Table 3 by parity 105 francs August 1914 (average) 97,50 francs June 1915 (average) 80,19 francs June 1916 (average) 66,75 francs June 1917 (average) 44,02 francs

fact: 摩拉维亚兹林的巴塔（Baťa）鞋厂在1914年有约400名员工，大战爆发后获得军方大批军靴订单并转产皮鞋，产量以百万双计；到1918年员工增至约4,000人（另一说4,100人），并自建制革厂、电厂与自有零售店。

sources.title: Nadace Tomáše Bati, “Company history”（巴塔基金会年表）
sources.quote: 1914 Thomas J. Bata was born the company had 400 employees and ranked among major footwear manufacturers in the country. After the outbreak of war, Bata company won extensive government contracts for military footwear and expanded production.

sources.title: City of Zlín (official), “The centre of the Baťa shoemaking empire”
sources.quote: The growth of production was sped up by World War I, when the Zlín factories were supplying millions of pairs of shoes to the Austro-Hungarian army. At the end of the war in 1918, the Baťa factory already had 4,000 employees.

sources.title: Bata's World, “Czech Republic”（Tomas Bata 基金会）
sources.quote: 1914–1918 – during the World War the number of employees rose to 4,100; the operations of the factory were reoriented to the production of leather shoes, supplying the army in particular.

fact: 巴塔公司在战后延续了战时的量产体系：1918—1920年员工一度回落至2,100人，1922年9月托马什·巴塔把鞋价下调一半，夺得捷克斯洛伐克鞋业市场主导；1938年公司员工总数达65,064人，其中海外23,250人。公司自1908年起为托马什·巴塔个人独资，当时并无公开交易的股份。

sources.title: City of Zlín (official), “The centre of the Baťa shoemaking empire”
sources.quote: in September 1922 he cut the price of his shoes by half and immediately won over thousands of customers with his cheap products. He gained control over the entire shoe market and became the shoe king in the then Czechoslovakia.

sources.title: City of Zlín (official), “The centre of the Baťa shoemaking empire”
sources.quote: In 1938 the Baťa Company had a total of 65,064 employees, 41,814 of them in Czechoslovakia and 23,250 abroad.

sources.title: Bata's World, “Czech Republic”（Tomas Bata 基金会）
sources.quote: Between 1918 and 1920 – post-war crisis – the number of employees of the factory fell to 2,100.
